data.narrative:
Lace Lithography is a Series A–stage semiconductor company that has raised $60M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductor players (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in chips and semiconductors, with particular relevance to same-stage private companies Rebellions ($2.3B), d-Matrix ($2.0B), and adjacent-stage Positron AI ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using the $60M raised as a value proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, implies a $120M valuation. Peer-median anchoring across the 3 same/adjacent-stage comps yields a $2.0B valuation, with the peer range spanning $1.0B to $2.3B. Public-comp P/S anchoring, while the semiconductor sector trades at a 18.9x median multiple, cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue data. 

The triangulated valuation range is $102M to $2.3B, with a median of $1.1B across the two applicable methods. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty: stage-progression relies on raised capital as a rough proxy for value creation, while peer-median anchoring assumes comparable risk and market timing. Resolution requires clarity on Lace Lithography's technical differentiation, IP position, and near-term revenue trajectory relative to the peer set.
